subject: Re: Subprocessor list & next steps — SOC 2 / GDPR questions
messages:

Cc: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@acmecorp.com>, legal@acmecorp.com
Date: 2027-04-25T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Subprocessor list & SOC 2 status (follow-up from call)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call today — helpful overview. As discussed, our security and procurement teams need the following to move forward with procurement:

- Full subprocessor list (cloud providers, analytics, monitoring, ML infra partners)
- Current SOC 2 status and expected timeline for next audit (if in progress)
- Confirmation on data sharing boundaries for customer data and whether any subprocessors see PII/data beyond encrypted tokens
- Vendor security questionnaire (we'll start it and share with legal)

Can you send the subprocessor CSV and SOC 2 summary, and let us know who at Redwood can own the vendor questionnaire? We'd like to close this by end of month.

Thanks,
Alice

Alice Johnson
Head of Procurement, AcmeCorp
alice.johnson@acmecorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-26T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor list & SOC 2 status (follow-up from call)

Hi Alice — great speaking with you and Tom yesterday. Per our call, attaching the current subprocessor export and a one-page SOC 2 summary. High-level notes below and next steps.

Attachments: [Attachment: subprocessor_list.csv (CSV, 7KB)], [Attachment: soc2_summary.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]

Quick recap / answers:
- Subprocessors: CSV includes cloud providers (AWS, GCP), monitoring (Datadog), error-tracking (Sentry), vector/embedding storage partners (VectorStoreCo), and a small set of managed infra partners.
- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II (security + availability) in 2025; the next audit window is scheduled for Q3 2027. We run continuous controls and can provide the SOC 2 report under NDA — let me know if you want the full report and I will coordinate.
- Data boundaries: Customer request routing, model execution, and KV cache are in our managed environment. We do not persist raw user inputs beyond retention windows unless configured by the customer; PII handling is governed by the customer contract and the data-processing addendum. See notes in CSV for subprocessors that handle telemetry/metrics vs. content.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll assign our security lead to the vendor questionnaire once you share the file (please confirm the questionnaire format — XLSX or Doc).
2) If you want the SOC 2 full report, confirm NDA recipient and I'll start the disclosure process.
3) We can schedule a short follow-up with our infra/security lead to walk through any flagged subprocessors.

Would Thursday 10–11am PT work for a 30-minute follow-up?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Team — forwarding Acme's request and my reply. They want: (1) full subprocessor CSV (done), (2) SOC 2 full report under NDA, (3) answers to vendor questionnaire.

Can you please:
- Aditya: review the CSV and flag any subprocessors that require contract/technical controls beyond standard (e.g., any third parties that store decrypted content or have potential to access raw inputs). Mark risks as High/Medium/Low in the sheet.
- Neha: I'll need you to own the vendor questionnaire once they send it — point person for responses and any evidence collection. If SOC 2 report is requested, you can coordinate the NDA and sharing.

Acme hopes to close by 4/30; let's prioritize this.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Subprocessor list & SOC 2 status — ACME procurement + questionnaire

Thanks Marissa — I pulled the CSV and did a first pass. Notes below (high-level):

- AWS (us-west-2) — primary compute + object storage; standard controls, encrypted at rest, does not access customer content. Risk: Low.
- GCP (us-east) — used for dedicated customers in region; Low.
- Datadog / Sentry — collect telemetry and stack traces; configured to redact user content by default. Risk: Medium — recommend adding contract obligation & evidence of redaction configs.
- VectorStoreCo — managed vector storage (caches embeddings). Risk: Medium-High — confirm encryption at rest/in-transit and key management; they do not have direct access to raw model inputs but hold embeddings.
- Third-party model optimizer vendor (OptiQuant) — only receives model binaries, not customer data. Risk: Low.

Action items for me: add risk column to the CSV and attach notes/evidence links (config screenshots, KMS docs). I can have the updated CSV back by EOD 4/29.

Aditya
